exam.title: CPE C++ Certified Entry-Level Programmer
exam.study_prerequisites: No formal prerequisite is published. Practice compiling, tracing, testing, and debugging small C++ programs across types and operators, stream state, control flow, functions and parameter mechanisms, arrays and vectors, pointers and object lifetimes, named casts, manual allocation, structures, and strings. Use at least C++11 for the named features in scope and verify the active version before purchase.

review.notes: All four CPE-20-01 blocks are mapped through translation and diagnostics, types/operators/streams, structured control and function calls, value/reference/pointer parameters and recursion, arrays/vectors/data pointers, named-cast purpose, manual allocation lifetime, structures and strings. Three integrated scenarios, eight hands-on labs and 40 original checks are included. Raw memory operations are taught for syllabus literacy while modern ownership is clearly related context. Nine links are reachable and O'Reilly/Udemy are automation-blocked; none are broken. The local objective monitor encountered a certificate-chain error after the same official page was fetched successfully by the source-health checker, so the exact public objective block was preserved manually and the transport discrepancy is documented. No recalled/live item, answer dump or copied course question is used.

findings.title: Hosted main arguments require a portable contract
findings.evidence: C++17 allows nonnegative argc, a null argv[argc], two portable int forms and special return 0 fallthrough. Platform-specific extensions are separate.
findings.recommendation: Add objective 1.3 argument/count/lifetime explanation and executed sentinel check.
findings.resolution: Add objective 1.3 argument/count/lifetime explanation and executed sentinel check.

findings.title: C++17 remainder sign is defined by truncating division
findings.evidence: N4659 specifies truncation toward zero and quotient/remainder identity when representable; older vendor wording suggests implementation-defined signs.
findings.recommendation: Teach and execute -11/4, -11%4 and 11%-4; exclude undefined division/overflow.
findings.resolution: Teach and execute -11/4, -11%4 and 11%-4; exclude undefined division/overflow.

findings.title: Successful integer extraction does not validate a complete line
findings.evidence: A public original program accepts 12 from 12x; the tested parser requires the remaining input to be whitespace/EOF and preserves the destination on rejection.
findings.recommendation: Add strict-line parsing, explicit domain checks and clear/consume recovery with streamsize limit.
findings.resolution: Add strict-line parsing, explicit domain checks and clear/consume recovery with streamsize limit.

findings.title: Both named pointer conversions are explicit objective 3.5
findings.evidence: The active 26-entry syllabus includes static_cast and dynamic_cast pointer conversions. Existing prose treated too much cast machinery as merely adjacent.
findings.recommendation: Add a minimal safe polymorphic hierarchy, success/null/failure checks and specific mappings for all 26 entries.
findings.resolution: Add a minimal safe polymorphic hierarchy, success/null/failure checks and specific mappings for all 26 entries.

findings.title: Container size and storage lifetime need separate traces
findings.evidence: Reserve does not create elements; reallocation invalidates stored addresses. C++17 string access has a distinct sentinel boundary.
findings.recommendation: Add executed reserve/resize/invalidation and string sentinel/at comparisons, discarding old pointers before reallocation.
findings.resolution: Add executed reserve/resize/invalidation and string sentinel/at comparisons, discarding old pointers before reallocation.

source_reading_boundaries.cpp17-multiplicative: Complete N4659 expr.mul clause read via public rendering. C++17 integer division truncates toward zero, paired remainder identity requires representable quotient, and zero/unrepresentable division is undefined. Small positive/negative cases actually executed; undefined cases deliberately excluded.
source_reading_boundaries.cpp17-string-access: Complete N4659 string.access clause read. operator[] permits read at size returning the null character, including empty string; non-null modification of sentinel is undefined. at(size) throws. Original code reads sentinel and catches checked failure, never writes or dereferences outside the contract.
source_reading_boundaries.cpp17-vector-capacity: Complete N4659 vector.capacity clause read. Reserve leaves size unchanged, reallocates when requested capacity exceeds old capacity and invalidates all prior element addresses. Append within sufficient reserved capacity preserves prior element references. Original code discards pointer before forced reallocation; exact growth factor not assumed.
source_reading_boundaries.cpp17-execution: Read N4659 execution text including implementation-defined/unspecified/undefined distinctions and sequencing paragraphs 14–18. Grouping differs from evaluation order; full-expression boundaries and conflicting unsequenced effects inform traces. Advanced abstract-machine examples were context, not executed or added syllabus.
source_reading_boundaries.cpp17-main: Complete N4659 main clause read. Portable int forms, nonnegative argc, conditional argv[0] meaning, null argv[argc] and special implicit return 0 support objective 1.3 repair. Original workbook uses parameter form and safely checks sentinel; it does not read private environment variables or host command-line secrets.
source_reading_boundaries.cpp17-ignore: Selected ignore paragraphs 25–27 and nearby getline/peek context read from N4659. Unlimited count uses numeric_limits<streamsize>::max(), and delimiter is extracted. Full unformatted stream chapter not audited. Tested recovery clears failure before consuming the line.
source_reading_boundaries.cpp17-string-io: Complete N4659 string.io clause read. Formatted extraction stops before whitespace; free getline extracts its delimiter without appending it. Original in-memory streams exercise numeric extraction, leftover newline and subsequent full name. Linked sentry and locale chapters not fully audited.

groups.title: Block 1 – Syntax, Literals, and Operators
objectives: 1.1 Identify valid C++ syntax elements, keywords, and code structures.
1.2 Recognize C++ built-in data types and corresponding literals.
1.3 Describe the structure and declaration of the main() function and its parameters.
1.4 Apply arithmetic, relational, logical, bitwise, and assignment operators.
1.5 Determine operator precedence, associativity, and the impact on expressions.
1.6 Apply short-circuit logic in control expressions.
1.7 Use basic input/output streams (cin, cout, cerr) and manipulators (endl, setw).

groups.title: Block 2 – Flow Control and Functions
objectives: 2.1 Describe and use conditional statements (if, else).
2.2 Use loop constructs (while, do, for) and loop control statements (break, continue).
2.3 Recognize the purpose of the goto statement and labeled statements.
2.4 Apply multiple-selection structures using switch, case, and default keywords.
2.5 Define, declare, and invoke functions with correct syntax.
2.6 Use return statements in typed and void functions.
2.7 Pass arguments by value, by reference, and by pointer.
2.8 Apply basic recursion to solve simple problems.

groups.title: Block 3 – Vectors and Pointers
objectives: 3.1 Declare, initialize, and manipulate vectors and arrays, including multidimensional arrays.
3.2 Access vector data using the data() method.
3.3 Declare and initialize pointers, including the use of nullptr.
3.4 Dereference pointers and use the address-of operator (&).
3.5 Perform pointer conversions using static_cast and dynamic_cast.
3.6 Manage dynamic memory with new, delete, and delete[].

groups.title: Block 4 – Structures and Strings
objectives: 4.1 Declare and define structures.
4.2 Access structure members using the dot (.) operator.
4.3 Declare vectors of structures and access their fields.
4.4 Declare, initialize, and manipulate std::string objects.
4.5 Perform basic string operations and comparisons.
